review.summary: approve_with_nits. Link checker: bad 0 (ran). make_toc --check and pytest were blocked by the sandbox; the script, tests and all seven contents lists were verified by reading, and CI (checks.yml) does run pytest. Top findings: (1) decision row PR6-F4 and the CHANGELOG say pyc untracking is deferred to a BACKLOG item, but commit 4c158d6 in this PR deletes all 17 pyc files and no BACKLOG item exists; (2) STYLE.md and README say a "↑ Contents" link sits before each lesson, but the first lesson of every week has none; (3) build() silently skips a week file whose first line is not a "# " title, so --check cannot flag it.

findings.checklist_item: REVIEW.md 'After the review': every decision is added to reviews/decisions.md; CHANGELOG has a line for the change
findings.title: PR6-F4 decision row and CHANGELOG say pyc untracking is deferred, but this PR does it
findings.claim: The PR6-F4 row says the untracking 'is left to the owner, as a BACKLOG item with the exact command', and the CHANGELOG line says 'untracking the pyc files is deferred'. Neither matches the diff: the PR deletes all 17 tracked .pyc files, and BACKLOG.md contains no such item (it was removed in the same commit). The log now points readers at a backlog entry that does not exist and under-reports what the PR changed.
findings.evidence: git show --stat 4c158d6: 'untrack bytecode', 20 files changed, deletes scripts/review_harness/__pycache__/*.pyc, providers/__pycache__/*.pyc, tests/__pycache__/*.pyc, tools/__pycache__/make_toc.cpython-313.pyc, and removes 1 line from BACKLOG.md. The PR diff shows the same deletions. BACKLOG.md on this branch has only the F8 and F7 items. CHANGELOG.md line 9: 'F4: .gitignore added; untracking the pyc files is deferred.'
findings.proposed_change: Per the log's own rule (never edit a decided row), add a superseding PR6-F4 row at the top: decision 'accept', reason '.gitignore added and the 17 tracked .pyc files removed in 4c158d6', Fixed in '#7'. Change the CHANGELOG F4 clause to 'F4 (.gitignore added, bytecode untracked)'. Test: git ls-tree -r HEAD --name-only | grep -c .pyc should print 0.

findings.checklist_item: STYLE.md 'Contents list'; 'Plain language: say things directly'
findings.title: STYLE.md and README say the back-link sits before each lesson; the first lesson has none
findings.claim: STYLE.md says every week file 'has a "↑ Contents" link before each lesson', and README says 'a "↑ Contents" link before each lesson takes you back to it'. make_toc.py writes the link only before every ## heading after the first lesson (the docstring says 'before every later "## " heading'), so lesson N.1 of each week has no link. A reader who looks for it at 1.1 will not find it.
findings.evidence: tools/make_toc.py build(): 'if first_lesson: first_lesson = False else: out += [BACK...]'. weeks/week-01-what-an-agent-is.md: no '[↑ Contents]' line precedes '## 1.1 LLM call vs workflow vs agent'; the first one precedes '## 1.2'. README.md line 9; STYLE.md line 58.
findings.proposed_change: STYLE.md: '...and a "↑ Contents" link before every lesson after the first, and before the week review.' README: 'a "↑ Contents" link before each later lesson takes you back to it.' No test needed; it is wording only.

findings.checklist_item: REVIEW.md E: tools/ scripts do what they claim
findings.title: build() silently returns a file unchanged when line 1 is not a title, so --check reports ok
findings.claim: If a week file does not start with '# ', build() returns the text untouched, main() sees new == old, and --check prints 'checked ok'. A new week file with a missing or misplaced title would therefore get no contents list and pass the check and test_week_contents_are_current without any signal. The docstring says the block goes 'right under the "# Week N — ..." title', so the absence of that title is an error condition, not a no-op.
findings.evidence: tools/make_toc.py lines 110-112: 'if not lines or not lines[0].startswith("# "): return text'. main() only reports files where new != old.
findings.proposed_change: Raise ValueError(f'first line must be a "# " title') in build() instead of returning text, so main() exits naming the file (the same path F5 added for an unclosed marker). Add a one-line test: toc.build('Intro\n## 9.1 X\n') raises ValueError.

findings.checklist_item: REVIEW.md E: tools/ scripts do what they claim
findings.title: make_toc.slug() strips link syntax from headings; check_links.slug() does not
findings.claim: make_toc.slug() first reduces '[text](url)' to 'text', matching GitHub, while check_links.py slug() keeps the URL characters. No current heading contains a link, so the parity test passes today, but the two scripts will disagree the first time one does, and check_links (the one CI trusts for anchors) would be the wrong one. The decision on F6 accepted a parity test instead of a shared function; this is the one known case where parity already does not hold.
findings.evidence: tools/make_toc.py line 49: re.sub(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r"\1", text). tools/check_links.py lines 4-7: strip, lower, remove [^\w\- ], replace spaces; no link stripping. tests/test_make_toc.py FIXTURE has no heading with a link.
findings.proposed_change: Either drop the link-stripping line from make_toc.slug() (keeping the two identical, since no heading has a link) or add a fixture heading with a link to test_anchors_match_check_links so the divergence is visible, and add the same re.sub to check_links.slug(). Test: the parity test on a fixture heading '## See [1.4](x.md)' must pass.
